items.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: I didn’t feel I had enough talent to be a Gerry Mulligan, who could write and play, or an Al Cohn, who could write and play the way I like to write and play

ctx.x: Indeed. But I wouldn’t have missed it for the world, having it taught to me like that. So I did that for a couple of years and then went to a private school called the American Operatic Laboratory, which I was studying composition there with a particular guy. I went there because this — he was approved by the Veterans. And there was a well known composer teaching there so I studied a bit with him. But actually I had to make a choice before I went there, because I didn’t feel I had enough talent to be a Gerry…
It’s interesting because other fellows have had similar decisions, like you mentioned Bill Holman, and he went the other way.
